prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. Editorial photograph for a top Scandinavian interiors magazine: the entrance hall of a Nordic garden house, 3 pm mid-winter, 24 mm shift lens at 1.2 m, level, straight verticals, all sharp. A threshold of light: the bright living room through the door on the left third, the console vignette on the right third.

2. LIGHT. The hall has no window. A frosted roof light just above the frame, over the bench, pours soft top light down the left wall. Exposed so the hall walls read soft warm white, about two thirds of a stop under the living room's back wall; the living room through the door is the brightest area, still detailed, lit from its tall north window on the left; its light spills a pale fan across the threshold floor and warms the edge of the oak portal. The facing wall darkens gently toward the right corner. Each piece has a lit left face and a right side about one stop darker, feathered shadows to the right and toward the camera, short contact shadows. The ceiling a touch darker than the walls, darkest at the top right. No sun patch. White balance 4600 K: warm white, never pink, yellow or grey; real contrast, never milky. One practical in the hall, 2700 K, no shadow: the cube wall lamp glows evenly through its faces and lays a soft warm fan on the wall around it.

3. MATERIALS. Matte mineral paint #F4F1EC, faint chalky movement. Wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E, running through the threshold. Bench, console and portal: oiled light oak #C8A27A with a soft satin sheen, one long soft highlight along the console top and down the planks toward the door; no mirror reflection.

4. PRODUCTS, exactly these:
a. ART above the console, centre x 0.68: a 45 x 55 portrait print, one loose black ink line on cream, wide cream mat, slim black wood frame, a little over half the console's length, no glare.
b. CONSOLE, right end: a matte textured warm-white ceramic vase, 26 cm, a third the height of the art, with 3-5 slender dried stems in sage and oat.
c. CONSOLE, middle: an empty slim oval tray in matte black metal, flat, a quarter of the console's length.
d. LEFT WALL at 1.7 m: four light pine oval pegs in a row, empty, no rail.
e. Above them: a 15 cm cube wall lamp in fine warm-white fabric, hand-span sized, hardwired, no cable.
f. BENCH, cut by the left edge: a warm off-white linen-look flat cushion, 3 cm thin; at the corner end a white cotton waffle throw folded into a neat square, the cushion's width.
g. Under the bench at the corner end: an empty 30 cm coiled rope basket, top third warm-white cotton, natural jute below, its rim below the seat.
h. Right of the console, cut by the bottom edge: a light natural-wood hexagonal umbrella bucket, half the console's height, one closed charcoal umbrella with a wooden handle.
i. THROUGH THE DOOR, the living room's own products only: three framed prints over the oatmeal sofa between two small travertine lamps, a cream braided rug, a glowing fabric lantern, a lit tripod floor lamp.

5. NOT IN FRAME: table lamp, mirror, boxes, plant, coats, bags, shoes, keys, books, glass, socket, cable, text, people. No bloom, haze, light rays, glow halos, HDR look, grain or vignette.

exposure.flag: DARK: needs more than +0.2 stop, not lifted further

grade.rule: docs/render-recipe-nordic-2026-10-24.md 2.6: WB on the hero-wall patch, exposure capped +-0.2 stop, chroma -10%, roll-off from L 94, S curve 0.12, black point to L 12.5 only if below 12, no grain, no vignette

clay_lock.method: regions = whole frame, quadrants, ceiling/floor bands and the clay boxes of fixed furniture / windows / openings; peaks below ~0.03 are unreliable (weak texture), so the verdict is visual (<aid>-lock.png) with the strong-peak number as support

verdict.note: portal, walls, console (dv -0.015) and the living vista (sofa, table, window, pendant) on the clay lines; the bench seat and the folded throw sit ~0.02-0.03 above the clay (weak peak 0.039); the upper-right 0.056 is a textureless-wall peak (0.007), not a shift

product_check.rule: each product inside its clay box +-15 % of the box size (<aid>-boxes.png); read visually

reading.living vista: pendant, curtains, sill vase, prints, wall-decor, accent sconce, cushions, runner, candles, bowl and rug all inside their boxes; tripod floor lamp lit
